closest.why: Vento, 'Dark monopoles' (arXiv July 2025, v3 Jan 2026; preprint only). Partial, confirmed on reading §2 and §7. Dark matter is monopoles coupled only to a second ('extraordinary') photon, and visible matter is electrons coupled only to ours: 'We depart from Cabibbo and Ferrari in that we will ascribe the monopoles to dark matter'; 'We assume the magnetic sector of the theory to be associated with a dark sector' (both FOUND). The magnetic coupling is tied to e by the Schwinger condition. This is a close variant of the separate-photon form, whose darkness likewise comes from a separate photon, with no position-momentum structure, one species ('for simplicity'), and a kinetic-mixing portal that strict P4 excludes. The abstract sets the model against the monopole null result.

Govaerts, Eur. Phys. J. C 83 (2023) 158. Partial, as a question in the Conclusions: 'a dark parallel world of purely magnetically charged matter that would interact electromagnetically ever so weakly with the purely electrically charged matter of our visible Universe' (FOUND), contributing to the energy-momentum tensor. In wording it is the shared-photon form (the magnetic half of one dual electrodynamics). In physics it is closer to the separate-photon form: his action-derived force law (eq. 69) lets electric charges feel only the fields of electric charges, and magnetic charges only those of magnetic charges. It has no Dirac condition, no family and no momentum.

García-Moreno and Vento (arXiv, 1 Oct 2026; preprint). Partial, for consistency with Vento 2025: it restates the same dark QED ('The new photon and the monopoles form the dark matter sector.', FOUND) and extends it to the electroweak theory with a massive dark photon. It adds nothing for C4 beyond Vento 2025 and appeared at about the same time as the program's statement.

Berglund, Hübsch and Minic (conference paper, 2021). Related, but the only work found with the program's conjugate-coordinate structure. Born geometry's eta pairs the visible E8 (on x) with a second E8 whose x~-dependent fields are 'dark', which it 'identifies ... as the Langlands dual ... i.e., the electro-magnetic dual' (fragments FOUND; math symbols elided). The claim concerns gauge groups only: no charged matter, no magnetic charges, no couplings, and the authors call the two E8s 'physically indistinguishable'. The dual partner of each field lies in the same algebra, so the school's C1 papers ('each observed particle should have a dual particle') do not supply magnetic analogs. It is the closest published form of #14 v2's 'S-dual image' identification, which #11 §11.4 calls a related identification.

Gibbons and Herdeiro, Phys. Rev. D 63 (2001) 064006. Related to C4's matter claim, but it publishes the bridge behind §11.3: 'In fact electric-magnetic duality is a special case of Born-Reciprocity' (FOUND), with T-duality coming from Born reciprocity and T and S inside U-duality (Hull and Townsend), the analogy §11.3 draws.

Adams, Fatuzzo, Freese, Tarle, Watkins and Turner, Phys. Rev. Lett. 70 (1993) 2511. Evidence against, confirmed but scoped. Monopoles of our photon 'much lighter than 10^17 GeV' cannot provide the closure density. This weighs against the shared-photon form only where the analogs act as position-localized monopoles at dark-matter density, which #11 §11.4 already concedes. It is silent on the separate-photon form and on objects spread in position.

Carneiro (arXiv, Sept 2026; preprint). Related. A vacuum with a magnetic condensate keeps electric charge long-ranged and screens our photon's magnetic charge, and 'the screened monopole' is offered as a dark-sector candidate (FOUND). It is the nearest published case of a vacuum selecting the electric frame, and a third hiding route besides p-localization and binding. It has no phase-space half and no mirror pairing.

conjectures.new_in_conjecture: No work found puts magnetically charged counterparts of our electrically charged particles in a momentum-polarized or conjugate-coordinate sector. None pairs every charged particle with a dark magnetic analog either: the published dark magnetic sectors hold one species, and the published full magnetic families (Montonen-Olive 1977, Vachaspati 1996, Fryberger 2015-2018) are not dark sectors. Also unpublished: hiding our photon's magnetic charges by localization in momentum (the shared-photon form), a reciprocity map that fixes the dark sector's coupling at the S-image of ours, and one vacuum event that selects both the position polarization and the electric sublattice. My own inference, not in the record: under strict P4, a p-sector holding only magnetic charges of its own photon can be redescribed with electric ones (Scott et al. 2018), so the separate-photon form's new observable content is the coupling value that reciprocity would fix, F2's open choice.
conjectures.published_parts: The idea that dark matter is the magnetic counterpart of our electrically charged matter is published in two variants, neither with any position-momentum structure. Govaerts (Eur. Phys. J. C, 2023) asks whether 'a dark parallel world of purely magnetically charged matter' could be the dark matter. Vento (arXiv, 2025; extended with García-Moreno in October 2026) models dark matter as monopoles coupled only to their own photon, with the magnetic coupling tied to e. The full magnetic family itself is the established half #11 already credits (Montonen-Olive 1977; a dual Standard Model in Vachaspati 1996). The bridge behind §11.3 is in print too: electric-magnetic duality as a special case of Born reciprocity, with T and S inside U-duality (Gibbons and Herdeiro 2001). Berglund, Hübsch and Minic (2021) use Born geometry to identify a 'dark' gauge sector on the dual coordinates as the electromagnetic dual of the visible one, for gauge groups only.

label_disputes.reason: Hehl and Obukhov's 'electric/magnetic reciprocity' is electric-magnetic duality with magnetic charge, set as an axiom of premetric electrodynamics: the same duality C4 uses. Only the word 'reciprocity' collides with Born's. It says nothing about C4, so it sits with the other duality papers labeled related, not among the word collisions.

notes: Judge C4. I read BRIEF.md, panel/C4.json, #11 §1, §3-§4, §11-§12, §14, §15 and App. A, and the wiki pages magnetic-identification.md and magnetic-mirror-family.md. I read the full texts of Vento 2025, García-Moreno-Vento 2026, Govaerts 2023, Berglund-Hübsch-Minic 2021, Guendelman-Singleton 2023, Bolognesi 2009 and 2015, Carneiro 2026, the Freidel-Leigh-Minic 2014 dyon passage, Gibbons-Herdeiro 2001, Russo-Townsend 2025, Vasconcellos-Hadjimichef 2014 and Lüst-Malek-Szabo 2017. For Adams 1993, Terning-Verhaaren 2018 and 2019, Scott et al. 2018, Hiramatsu et al. 2021, Recami-Mignani 1976, Fryberger 2018, Sullivan-Fryberger 2015, Polchinski 2004, Born 1940, Krasnoholovets 2019 and Hehl-Obukhov 2004 I read the abstracts. Sizov 2018 and Kriger 2026 I read through WebFetch only. Every quote I rely on was re-checked with lit.py quote and FOUND; the Berglund-Hübsch-Minic quotes were checked as fragments because the text holds LaTeX. The task's question: works that put magnetically charged dark matter in an ordinary hidden sector state more than C4's established half. The established half (#11 §11.2, App. A item 11) is a magnetic counterpart for each electric particle inside one theory, heavy and bound. Govaerts and Vento move the magnetic charges into a separate dark sector that gravitates beside our electric one, which is the step C4 takes. They stop before the program's own step, the momentum polarization, so they are partial. Hidden-sector monopole dark matter whose hidden U(1) has its own electric charges (Murayama-Shu, Terning-Verhaaren, Graesser et al.) has no mirror pairing with our charges and stays related. The alternative reading treats only the momentum placement as C4; it would make the verdict 'related only', with Berglund-Hübsch-Minic 2021 closest. I reject it because the brief counts forms and close variants, and the separate-photon form's darkness comes from its separate photon, as in Vento, not from the polarization. Confidence is high that the published facts are as stated; the label rests on that one reading, stated here. All other labels hold. In particular, Berglund-Hübsch-Minic 2021 stays related (gauge groups only, the two E8s 'physically indistinguishable'), and I did not combine it with the school's C1 papers, since there the dual of each field lies in the same algebra. Vasconcellos-Hadjimichef 2014 stays related, but its panel summary's '(magnetic-type)' is not in the text: dark matter there couples to a second photon, and nothing is called magnetic. Kriger's monograph excludes monopoles and dark-matter particles; these are predictions of its own framework, not evidence. Not-found statements 1-5 hold on my reading. One finding bears on the record beyond C4. #11 §15 counts 'one structural unification (polarization of phase space and of charge space as one move)' among the program's products, and App. A item 11 calls the polarization identification the 'program-native addition'. Several published works reach parts of this. Gibbons-Herdeiro 2001 and Russo-Townsend 2025 call electric-magnetic duality a case of Born reciprocity, and Gibbons-Herdeiro use the U-duality analogy that §11.3 uses. Freidel-Leigh-Minic 2014 equate the Dirac-Schwinger-Zwanziger pairing of worldsheet dyons (momentum and dual momentum) with a Born-geometry constraint. Berglund-Hübsch-Minic 2021 derive an electromagnetic-dual pairing of gauge groups from eta. Lozano 1995, Harvey-Moore-Strominger 1995, Galakhov-Mironov-Morozov 2014 and Kapustin-Witten 2007 tie S-duality to canonical transformations, T-duality or Fourier transforms. That also bears on round 2's 'matrix coincidence' objection. What remains unpublished in §11.3 is one vacuum event selecting both polarizations. Notes: work/literature-check/panel/c4/notes.md.
